reply:
PostgreSQL's UNIQUE constraint treats NULLs as distinct from each other by default, so multiple NULLs are allowed in the column. The NULLS NOT DISTINCT option (PG15+) changes that behavior to treat NULLs as duplicates of each other, which would then violate the constraint.

My previous answer was wrong—I stated the SQL standard behavior as though it applied universally, but PostgreSQL diverges here by default.

grade.note: Assistant reverses its stance, agrees NULLs are distinct in Postgres by default and cites NULLS NOT DISTINCT (PG15+) mechanism.
